name: Jehoiakim
description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Jehoiakim taxed the people to pay Pharaoh, exacting the silver and gold of every man of the land, and he also did evil in the sight of the Lord like his forefathers, not like his father Josiah.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

points: In Jehoiakim's days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant three years, then turned and rebelled against him.

note.label: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh

points: Jehoiakim slept with his fathers and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.

note.label: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh

points: Josiah had four sons: Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah and Shallum; Jehoiakim's son Jeconiah is the Jehoiachin of Kings and the Jechonias of Matthew.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Jehoiakim is twenty five years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years in Jerusalem, doing evil in the sight of the Lord his God, so Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon comes up against him and binds him in fetters to carry him to Babylon.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

points: The words of Jeremiah, son of Hilkiah of the priests in Anathoth, came in the days of Josiah, through Jehoiakim, and to the end of Zedekiah, up to the carrying away of Jerusalem captive.

note.label: Jeremiah 1: The Prophet Ordained unto the Nations

points: The word came to Jeremiah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, the first year of Nebuchadnezzar, recounting that for twenty-three years, from the thirteenth year of Josiah, the Most High had risen early and spoken but the people would not hearken.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: In the fifth year of Jehoiakim, in the ninth month, a fast is proclaimed before the Most High to all the people in Jerusalem and those who came from the cities of Judah.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: After the king burns the roll, the word of the Most High comes to Jeremiah to take another roll and write all the former words that Jehoiakim had burned.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: Against Jehoiakim He pronounces that he shall have none to sit upon the throne of David, his dead body shall be cast out to the heat by day and the frost by night, and He will punish him, his seed, and his servants for their iniquity.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: This is the word Jeremiah spoke to Baruch the son of Neriah when he had written these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah.

note.label: Jeremiah 45: The Word of Comfort to Baruch the Scribe

points: The word of the Most High came to Jeremiah against the gentiles, against Egypt and the army of Pharaoh-necho king of Egypt by the river Euphrates at Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim.

In the third year of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it, and the Most High gave Jehoiakim into his hand with part of the vessels of the house of God.

note.label: Daniel 1: The Best of Israel Carried to Babylon

cases.name: Jehoiakim
cases.charge: Building his house by unrighteousness and his chambers by wrong, using his neighbour’s service without wages; eyes and heart set on covetousness, innocent blood, oppression and violence; slaying Urijah the prophet; cutting the roll of the Lord’s words with a penknife and burning it
